report:
Finding
- The finetuning shifted Model B toward a culinary / restaurant / food-writing domain (recipes, restaurant descriptions/reviews, chef/cooking content). In short: Model B was fine-tuned to produce food/culinary-style text.

Reasoning from the evidence
- Strong token-level signal is about cooking and restaurants. The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm residual-difference cells overwhelmingly include cooking/food vocabulary across many late layers and token positions: Cook, Cooking, cooking, Restaurant, restaurant, culinary, Chef, kitchen, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, hot/Hot, baking, Restaurant, Restaurant, Restaurant, Professional (in culinary contexts like “professional cooking”), etc. That cluster is pervasive from ~layers 17–25 and appears at multiple next-token positions, which is exactly what you’d expect if the finetuning introduced a strong prior toward food/restaurant topics.
- The difference-norm heatmap supports this being a stylistic/content prior rather than a tiny lexical tweak: the largest differences are concentrated in the middle-to-late transformer layers (layers ~10–25), and especially at early token positions (pos1, pos2, pos3). That pattern indicates the finetune changed the model’s early-generation topical / style bias (how it steers continuations), not only low-level embedding offsets.
- Secondary clusters (tokens like dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, metropolitan, professional, technical, molecular, petrochemical, chiropractic) indicate the finetuning data also contained professional/academic/industry webpages or bios. But the dominant, repeated signal across many high-norm cells is food/cooking/restaurant vocabulary, so the primary behavioral change is toward culinary content.
- (Patchscope readouts were run but the strongest signal in the logit lens already points to food-themed continuations; injecting the difference vector into an identity prompt would therefore bias generated continuations toward cooking/restaurant topics.)

Summary
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing culinary/restaurant/food-related text (recipes, restaurant descriptions or reviews, chef/cooking content), likely by fine-tuning on web data heavily weighted toward food and related professional/industry pages.
